title: CT learning detects gastric cancer downstaging after chemotherapy
summary: Linear support-vector models analyzed baseline and restaging CT in a retrospective 292-patient gastric-cancer study. Models were evaluated in two separate testing cohorts against downstaging defined by baseline clinical and postoperative pathological stages; restaging AUCs were 0.922 and 0.850. The study did not demonstrate improved surgical decisions, and selected images, small same-centre tests and inconsistent abstract cohort labels limit interpretation.
ai_technology: Linear support-vector classifier; radiomic feature selection

source_review.scope: Primary relevant model Methods, Results and limitations; exact primary identity and current primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: Model development with nested cross-validation, followed by two held-out same-centre clinical testing cohorts and a postoperative pathology-based stage reference.
evidence.unknown: Prospective decision benefit and multicentre generalization remain unestablished; clinical baseline staging can be inaccurate, and low-quality images were excluded.
evidence.ai_role: Linear support-vector classifiers learn relationships between selected CT texture features and recorded post-chemotherapy downstaging.
